title: Finite pushforward preserves upper weights
statement:
If $g:Z_0\to Y_0$ is finite and
$K\in D_{\le w}(Z_0)$, then $Rg_*K=Rg_!K$ belongs to
$D_{\le w}(Y_0)$.

proof.text: Use the separated finite-type finite-field and coefficient conventions implicit in $D_{\le w}$ of [def-weil-complex-weights]. Let $g:Z\to Y$ be the geometric base change of $g:Z_0\to Y_0$. The schemes $Z,Y$ are separated of finite type over $k$ by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Finiteness survives each base change used here: on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, finite module generators $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $B$ give generators $b_1\otimes1,\ldots,b_r\otimes1$ of $B\otimes_A A'$ over $A'$; the fibre-product affine charts therefore satisfy [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. This applies both to $g$ and to the finite fibre in Step 3. A finite morphism is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. The properness clause of [prop-functor-package] gives $Rg_!\simeq Rg_*$. This is an isomorphism of Weil complexes by [prop-weil-operations], so it suffices to prove the upper weight bound for $Rg_*K$.

source.place: First sentence: finite is proper and Rg_!=Rg_*

proof.text: By [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image], $Rg_*$ is $t$-exact on the actual rational constructible categories and $\mathcal H^j(Rg_*K)\simeq g_*^c\mathcal H^j(K)$. The naturality of these identifications and the Weil lifts of [prop-weil-operations] make them identifications of Weil sheaves. Fix $j$. The definitions [def-weil-complex-weights, def-weil-punctual-weights] give a finite filtration $0=F_0\subset\cdots\subset F_m=\mathcal H^j(K)$ by constructible Weil subsheaves, with quotients $Q_i$ punctually pure of weights $u_i\le w+j$. Exactness of $g_*^c$ sends $0\to F_{i-1}\to F_i\to Q_i\to0$ to a short exact sequence. Thus the images of the $g_*^cF_i$ form a finite Weil filtration with quotients $g_*^cQ_i$; no splitting or semisimplicity is used.

source.place: First sentence through exactness pushes the filtration forward

proof.text: Fix one quotient $Q=Q_i$ of weight $u=u_i$, and a closed point $y\in Y_0$ with $q_y=\#\kappa(y)$. Restrict $Q$ to the finite scheme $T_0=Z_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$; its Weil structure relative to $\kappa(y)$ is the $[\kappa(y):k_0]$-fold iterate of the original structure, with the point transport prescribed by [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. By [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image], the stalk $(g_*^cQ)_{\bar y}$ is the geometric sections of this fibre, and its evaluation maps to the source stalks are natural under semilinear isomorphisms. The Weil direct-image structure is the exchange map followed by the image of the Weil structure, by [prop-weil-operations]; hence on these evaluation maps its local operator $F_y$ is precisely the geometric Frobenius of the finite fibre over $\kappa(y)$. The structure morphism of the finite geometric fibre is finite, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]; the properness comparison of [prop-functor-package] identifies its ordinary and compactly supported sections, compatibly with the Weil action by [prop-weil-operations]. Apply [lem-a1-finite-weil-sections-decomposition] with base field $\kappa(y)$. For each closed $x$ over $y$ it gives an invariant block $V_x$ consisting of $f_x=[\kappa(x):\kappa(y)]$ stalks, cyclically permuted by $F_y$, and on each stalk the return $F_y^{f_x}$ is the local $F_x$. The latter normalization agrees with the original base $k_0$: iterating $[\kappa(y):k_0]$ a total of $f_x$ times is the defining $[\kappa(x):k_0]$-fold iterate. This uses geometric stalks, with no arithmetic Frobenius invariants.

source.place: Finite stalk formula and Frobenius cycles, with relative residue degree and point transport made explicit

proof.text:
Let $\mu$ be an eigenvalue of $F_y$ on a nonzero block $V_x$ of Step 3. Choose an eigenvector $v\ne0$. Then $F_y^{f_x}v=\mu^{f_x}v$. Choose a nonzero stalk component $v_z$ of $v$. The return identity on that component gives $F_xv_z=\mu^{f_x}v_z$, so $\mu^{f_x}$ is an eigenvalue of the local operator on $Q_{\bar x}$. By [def-weil-punctual-weights] and purity of $Q$, $|\iota(\mu^{f_x})|=q_x^{u/2}$. The field extension has degree $f_x$, hence $q_x=q_y^{f_x}$ (a basis gives $f_x$ coordinates over the $q_y$-element field). Therefore
$$|\iota(\mu)|^{f_x}=q_y^{f_xu/2}.$$
Since $f_x\ge1$ and $q_y>0$, taking the positive $f_x$-th root gives $|\iota(\mu)|=q_y^{u/2}$. For an eigenvector on the whole finite direct sum, a nonzero block component is still an eigenvector with the same eigenvalue; thus this proves the assertion for every eigenvalue on $(g_*^cQ)_{\bar y}$. If the fibre or stalk is zero there is no eigenvalue to check. Consequently $g_*^cQ$ is punctually pure of weight $u$.

source.place: Displayed absolute-value calculation; elementary eigenvector argument on cyclic blocks

proof.text: Step 4 applies to every quotient of the filtration from Step 2. Its pushed-forward quotients are therefore punctually pure of weights $u_i\le w+j$, so $g_*^c\mathcal H^j(K)$ is mixed of weights at most $w+j$ by [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Zero quotients can be omitted; the zero sheaf has the empty filtration. For every $j$, Step 2 identifies this sheaf with $\mathcal H^j(Rg_*K)$, and [def-weil-complex-weights] gives $Rg_*K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$. The Weil isomorphism of Step 1 gives the same conclusion for $Rg_!K$.

source.place: Final two sentences: mixed sheaf bound and the cohomological definition of D_le_w
